analysis.overall: You spent 85% of the day in range with stable numbers overnight, though a delayed rise after breakfast caused a late-morning peak.

events.title: Smooth afternoon drift
events.description: Lunch insulin gently brought you down to a low point of 75 mg/dL. Your pump throttled back basal delivery, allowing you to level off safely without needing extra carbs.

events.title: Post-dinner creep
events.description: After your 40g dinner, glucose steadily climbed to a peak of 203 mg/dL. It took several small micro-corrections over a few hours to work it back down into range.

events.title: Dawn rise corrected
events.description: A brief early morning rise pushed you up to 157 mg/dL, but prompt small boluses brought you back down to a steady 90–100 mg/dL well before breakfast.

events.title: Delayed breakfast spike
events.description: Your 60g breakfast bolus initially caused a quick drop to 94 mg/dL before the food hit, triggering a sharp surge up to 246 mg/dL that required several correction doses to turn around.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Watch out for a delayed curve at breakfast—if insulin acts faster than your food absorbs, you might see an initial drop followed by a late spike.
